assessment: Ready for retained-SDK offline build recovery and portable-binary regeneration on the tested Debian Bookworm x86_64 host, using the documented combined-SDK Python installation step.

dependency_preservation.application_source: Matching repository source vendors FLTK and selected Rev modules/resources, GLM/NanoSVG, XZ/liblzma, QR and LDPC. Native SDK supplies compiler/build tools and target development/runtime dependency closure.
dependency_preservation.native_source_replay: Retained source archive contains resolved host/target downloads, pinned Buildroot, helpers, recipe, patches and checksums; cold replay still requires an existing bootstrap compiler and ordinary host utilities and was not retested here.
dependency_preservation.portable_host_requirements: glibc2.36+, compatible kernel, display facilities/fonts, graphics drivers/capabilities for Rev, and ALSA configuration/plugins/devices.
dependency_preservation.rev_redistribution: Verbal redistribution agreement between mirage335 and upstream Rev developer confirmed; accepted as resolved for this readiness assessment.

wasm_recovery.path: Use retained native SDK Python only for Wasm install, then stock Bookworm host tools for application/package tests

serial_retries.harness_interruption: Original retry driver stopped after four completed steps because its scratch-directory glob also selected the earlier non-GUI verification copy. No runtime test was launched by the failed precondition. Resume only pending copied test using exact original fatal-failure root.

complete_portable.scope: Existing release-web library assembly and full non-GUI copied-package/ABI checks; no publication and no replacement of original producers. GUI reception evidence remains from original exact native executable bytes.

findings.fact: Native retained source/binary inventory verification, SDK install/host ABI verification and FLTK/Rev portable TGZ+ZIP production with non-GUI copied-package checks passed without an ambient compiler or external network.

Tested Bookworm Python3.11.2 fails Wasm install at TarFile.extract(filter=...). Retained native SDK Python installs it offline; stock Bookworm CMake3.25/Ninja1.11 then built and packaged Wasm. This combined-SDK install route is not automatically selected by --wasm-sdk.

Original native web group12/13 failed playback underrun. Idle originalNode18 and archivedNode24 same-worker Live retries pass, and fullNode24 native web13/13 passes. Original failure remains preserved; no cause is established.

Wasm web4/5 failed initially with playback underrun during overlapping compilation. Idle fullWasm group also4/5 fails, at48000Hz after180sec RX because second consumed-microphone-level response missed2000ms. Subsequent incoming-message/pending-identity/physical-absence assertions and44100Hz scenario were not reached. Overlap and Node18 cannot explain all failures.
Original copiedFLTK TGZ GUI phase21 received only the final17 of32 raw Help bits. Exact same extracted package was retried on idle host; original fatal failure and fixture remain retained.

Rev source4/5 cases passed; GUI reported progressing typed workload limit at600sec. CopiedRev TGZ likewise reported incomplete workload coverage. Direct local ctest/verifier exited nonzero. CI uses a separate validated warning classifier and Mesa thread limits; this experiment is not a green CI-equivalent Rev smoke pass. ZIP GUI scopes were not reached.

Existing release-web APIs assembled the serial-tested Wasm bytes into fresh native FLTK/Rev archive pairs offline. All original native bytes/modes remained identical; complete archive inventory/provenance, copied CLI/frontend/dependency closure and glibc2.36 ABI checks passed. GUI evidence remains from those exact unchanged native executable bytes.

Windows dependency base requires separately supplied Microsoft v143 compiler19.44.35229/linker14.44.35229 or newer and Windows SDK. A complete saved Microsoft offline installer layout was not restored here. Current Microsoft supported build-host requirements do not justify a blanket old-Windows assurance.

limits: No full source cold SDK/compiler reconstruction in this experiment; Wasm compiler/Binaryen/Node inputs are retained upstream binaries.
No fresh Windows or ARM64 build recovery, physical audio/browser hardware tests, full modem calibration/regression or new release certification.
Published certified release is an earlier exact source/inventory; tested source has only lightweight automatic CI plus these independent diagnostic scopes.
Original overlap was a diagnostic scheduling mistake; serial outcomes are separate evidence and do not erase failures.

existing_ci.published_result: passed_with_warnings; recognized Windows WGL graphics omissions; no claim of fresh full current-HEAD certification

private_full_evidence_archive.contains: Complete logs/configuration, produced portable archives and original synthetic failed GUI fixture; no API token/private SSH key.

readiness_scope.standard: Reasonably available Debian Bookworm distro packages, reasonably recent Microsoft freeware build tools, adequate hardware and working devices/drivers are expected host prerequisites.
readiness_scope.demonstrated: Offline native/Wasm build recovery and complete portable bundle regeneration using retained source/binary SDK resources, without project redevelopment.
readiness_scope.installation_step: Use retained native SDK Python to install Wasm SDK on the tested Bookworm Python3.11.2 host; no newer OS or upstream download required after staging.
readiness_scope.qualification_limits: Hardware-intensive GUI/simulation/live workloads retain their measured failures or incomplete coverage. Less intensive coverage and CLI/FLTK alternatives support recovery readiness; no hardware-only cause is established. Windows older-host restoration was not performed here; existing CI covers its prepared dependency recipe and separately supplied Microsoft tools.
